home.asio_audio_device: An ASIO audio device is needed
home.keep_latency_low: To keep latency low, gachi sends and receives sound through ASIO only. No ASIO driver was found on this PC.
home.install_asio_driver: Install the ASIO driver from your audio interface maker's website, then check again. If you use a DAW, choose VST link in Settings → Audio, and the app needs no ASIO device of its own.
home.rooms_open_same: Rooms open on the same router show up here
home.dont_see_room: Don't see a room that was just made? Press refresh
home.password_room_rejoins: Password room (rejoins with the password you used)
room.bars_counted_before: Bars counted before it starts (a higher click)
room.off_bpm_time: On/off, BPM, time and count-in apply to the whole room. The volume is yours alone.
room.format_cant_change: The format can't change while recording.
room.sound_going_back: Their sound is going back to them: the others hear themselves again. Please check your input connections.

room.couldnt_open_wanted: Couldn't open '{wanted}', so '{used}' is used instead. Check that no other program is using the device.
room.cant_open_vst: Can't open the VST link ({e}). If gachi is running twice, close one.
room.cant_open_asio: Can't open the ASIO device ({e}). If another program (a DAW, say) is using it, close it and try again. The driver may allow only one program at a time.
room.asio_format_not: This ASIO driver hands out sound in a sample format gachi can't read (3-byte 24 bit, or 64 bit float). If the driver's settings offer 32 bit or 16 bit, switch to that. If not, use the DAW connection mode (the gachi plugin).

room.room_code_12: The room code was on for 12 hours, so it was turned off. The jam goes on. To invite more people, turn the code back on in the room settings.
room.name_runs_theirs: {name} runs at {theirs} Hz and you at {ours} Hz, so the sound is converted. Matching rates sound best.
room.host_turned_room: The host turned the room code on. Anyone with the code can join.
room.host_turned_room_code: The host turned the room code off. No one new can join now.
room.lost_connection_name: Lost the connection to {name}. Waiting for it to come back.
room.connection_dropped_waiting: Your connection dropped. Waiting for it to come back.
room.audio_device_reconnected: The audio device reconnected, so the recording was saved and stopped.
room.audio_device_settings: The audio device settings changed, so it was opened again: {summary}
room.audio_device_stopped: The audio device stopped, so it was opened again: {summary}
room.audio_device_stopped_please: The audio device stopped. Please check its connection ({e})
room.audio_device_not: The audio device is not open
room.connection_server_not: The connection to the server is not encrypted (ws://). Join requests are sealed on their own, but who joins which room can be seen.
room.another_program_using: Another program is using the fixed port {port}, so an automatic port is used this time. If this keeps happening, choose another number in Settings.
room.connection_server_not_answering: The connection server is not answering. Please try again in a moment.
room.host_not_answering: The host is not answering. Please try again in a moment.
room.couldnt_verify_hosts: Couldn't verify the host's answer (security check failed). Please try again.
dialog.room_has_password: This room has a password. Enter the one the host gave you.
dialog.invite_link_once: from this invite link? Once you join, the people in the room hear you. If you don't know this link, close this.
dialog.get_installer_download: Get the installer from the download page and run it: you'll have the new version with your settings as they are.
dialog.only_host_change: Only the host can change these.
dialog.if_everyone_sees: If everyone sees the same numbers, no one is listening in between.
settings.audio_interface_drivers: The audio interface driver's settings (buffer size, sample rate)
settings.real_latency_buffer: The real latency: the buffer plus USB transfer and the driver's safety margin
settings.make_sound_bar: Make a sound and a bar rises on the channel the signal comes in on. With 'Mic + stereo' you can send your mic and a loopback (PC sound) together. Don't pick a loopback whose bar rises with the test tone: that channel carries this app's output (the others' sound), so they would hear themselves back.
settings.only_hear_click: Only you hear the click; it isn't sent to the others.
settings.show_my_room: Show my room on the same network
settings.when_host_room: When you host, your room appears on the home screen of people on the same router (Wi-Fi or wired). Only while the code is on, and never on other networks.
settings.auto_sends_one: Auto sends one packet per device buffer (split evenly above 64). Picking by hand, smaller is faster but means more upload packets, and going below the device buffer doesn't make it faster.
settings.what_favor_when: What to favor when the connection stalls now and then. 'Fast' keeps the buffer small and fills the stalls by patching the sound (latency ↓, short gaps ↑). 'Steady' grows the buffer to prevent them (latency ↑, gaps ↓). On an even connection all three are the same.
settings.auto_keeps_each: Auto keeps each person at the smallest size without dropouts. You can also press the latency number on someone's card to adjust theirs.
settings.turn_when_router: Turn this on when your router has no UPnP or it's off. On the router's admin page, forward this UDP port to this PC. Other PCs on the same router need different numbers. Applies from the next room you join.
settings.draws_window_graphics: Draws the window with the graphics card. If the screen flickers or breaks up, turn it off. Sound and encryption (AES-256) are not affected. Applies after a restart.
settings.check_new_version: Check for a new version at start
settings.start_app_asks: At start, the app asks GitHub once whether a new version is out. If there is one, the home screen only says so; nothing is downloaded or installed by itself. While asking, GitHub can see your internet address (IP).
settings.turn_only_when: Turn on only when looking into a problem. Off, the log keeps brief events; on, it records the connection in detail every 2 seconds. Logs stay on this PC (the last 5) and are never sent anywhere. Names, chat and passwords are never logged.
settings.low_latency_p2p: Low-latency P2P jamming with friends over the internet
settings.gachi_free_software: gachi is free software. Under the GNU General Public License version 3 (GPLv3), anyone may use, change and redistribute it. It comes as is, without any warranty. The full license is in the LICENSE file installed with the program.
settings.sound_chat_go: Sound and chat go encrypted directly (P2P) between the people in a room, never through a server. The connection server only introduces rooms and doesn't keep who connected (internet addresses included). While connecting, though, the connection server, its operator and Cloudflare, which hosts it, can see your internet address (IP). And since the connection is direct, people in the same room can find each other's IP.
settings.font_pretendard_sil: Fonts: Pretendard and Pretendard JP (SIL Open Font License 1.1). gachi also uses open source libraries under the MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses, such as Tauri, cpal, Tokio, rustls, RustCrypto (ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-GCM, X25519) and vst3.
settings.others_sound_getting: ⚠ The others' sound is getting back into the gachi plugin's input and going back to them. In the DAW, keep gachi's output (or a multi-output track, a loopback) from reaching the gachi plugin.
settings.others_sound_getting_back: ⚠ The others' sound is getting back into your input and going back to them. A loopback channel may be picked as input, or the speakers may be reaching the mic. Use headphones or change the input channel.
settings.gachi_plugin_several: The gachi plugin is on several tracks. Only the first one on sends sound; the rest pass it through. Group the tracks to send into one group track and put a single plugin at its end.
settings.about_mb_mbps: about {mb} Mbps for this room ({n} people),
settings.sent_uncompressed_0: Sent uncompressed (0 ms codec delay). Upload needed: {here}about {a} Mbps for an 8-person room, about {b} Mbps for 16.
settings.higher_quality_pick: For higher quality, pick 24-bit (about 1.4× the upload).
settings.device_latency_estimated: Device latency (estimated from the DAW's block)
settings.device_latency_buffer: Device latency (from the buffer; the driver doesn't say)
settings.change_daws_audio: Change them in the DAW's audio settings and they show here.
settings.change_sample_rate: Change the sample rate and buffer size in the control panel (the button above, or the maker's app); they show here within seconds.
settings.daw_uses_audio:
The DAW uses the audio interface, and the gachi plugin sends and receives the sound. Gather the tracks to send into a group track and put the gachi plugin at its very end. Sample rate and buffer follow the DAW's settings.
Get the plugin (gachi, VST3) separately from the download page and put it in your DAW's VST3 folder. Open download page
settings.gachi_opens_asio: gachi opens the ASIO device itself. To use it alongside a DAW, choose VST link (drivers often allow only one program).
app.codes_never_use: Codes never use 0, O, 1, I or L

app.room_created_share: Room created. Share the code to invite friends.

latency.lots_packet_loss: Lots of packet loss. Try one step more jitter buffer.
metro.turn_off_metronome: Turn off the metronome · {bpm} BPM · {sig} (whole room)

rec.one_stereo_track_about: One stereo track is about {size} an hour. Lossless, and any DAW opens it.

direct.network_seems_block: Your network seems to block direct connections (UDP), as at work, school or public Wi-Fi. Try your home internet or another network.
direct.name_s_network: {name}'s network seems to block direct connections (UDP), as at work, school or public Wi-Fi. {name} could try home internet or another network.
direct.youre_same_router: You're on the same router but can't connect. A firewall or antivirus on one of the PCs may be blocking gachi. On both PCs, check that gachi is allowed in the Windows Security firewall settings.
direct.both_share_same: You both share the same public address (a provider's shared address, or one building's internet). Such networks often block connections between the people inside. It may work if one of you switches networks, or if you both have IPv6.
direct.youre_both_internet: You're both on internet that makes direct connections hard (mobile hotspot, work network and the like). If even one of you switches to home internet (wired or router Wi-Fi), it may connect.
direct.internet_makes_direct: Your internet makes direct connections hard (mobile hotspot, work network and the like). It may connect if you switch to home internet (wired or router Wi-Fi), or turn on UPnP on your router (or, without it, forward the fixed port from Settings).
direct.name_s_internet: {name}'s internet makes direct connections hard (mobile hotspot, work network and the like). It may connect if {name} switches to home internet (wired or router Wi-Fi), or if you turn on UPnP on your router (or, without it, forward the fixed port from Settings).
direct.both_connections_normally: Both of your connections normally allow direct connections. A firewall or antivirus on one of the PCs may be blocking gachi. On both PCs, check that gachi is allowed in the Windows Security firewall settings, and try turning on UPnP on the router (or, without it, forward the fixed port from Settings).
direct.name_s_internet_may: {name}'s internet may make direct connections hard (mobile hotspot, work network and the like), or a firewall on one of the PCs may be blocking gachi. {name} could switch to home internet, or you could turn on UPnP on your router.
